title: Rain Does Not Fall on One Roof Alone
proverb: Rain does not fall on one roof alone.
literal_meaning: When rain falls from the sky, it does not choose only one house. It falls on many roofs in the community.
deeper_meaning: Life's events, whether good or bad, rarely affect only one person. Human beings are connected, and the actions, successes, mistakes, and struggles of one person can influence the entire community.
historical_background: The Akan people of Ghana have a rich tradition of using proverbs as a way of teaching wisdom, morality, and social responsibility. In traditional Akan societies, people lived in close communities where farming, trade, leadership, and family relationships depended on cooperation. Rain was a powerful symbol because agriculture and survival depended on it.
cultural_significance: Among the Akan, rain represents blessings, change, and events that touch everyone. The proverb reminds people that nobody exists separately from society. A person's actions can bring either benefit or harm to the wider community.

story.title: The Farmer Who Thought the Drought Belonged Only to Others
story.content:
Long ago in an Akan village, there lived a wealthy farmer named Kwame. He owned many fields and had stored enough food to survive several months. Because his own barns were full, he believed that the problems of other villagers were not his concern.

One year, the rains arrived late. Many farmers struggled because their crops were failing. The village elders asked successful farmers to share seeds and knowledge with those who were suffering.

Kwame refused. He said, 'My fields are healthy. The drought belongs to them, not to me.'

The elders warned him, 'Rain does not fall on one roof alone. When one part of the village suffers, everyone is affected eventually.'

Kwame ignored their advice. As the months passed, the drought became worse. The farmers who had lost their crops could no longer trade, buy tools, or support the local market. Soon, even Kwame's business began to suffer because the entire village economy had weakened.

Realizing his mistake, Kwame gathered the community and offered help. The villagers worked together, shared seeds, repaired farms, and prepared for the next planting season.

After the harvest returned, Kwame thanked the elders for their wisdom.

The oldest elder said, 'A village is like many roofs under the same sky. When rain comes, every roof receives it. When hardship comes, every person feels it.'

life_lessons: Everyone is connected to the community around them.
Ignoring other people's problems can create bigger problems later.
Sharing knowledge and resources strengthens society.
A person's success should benefit others.
Unity helps communities survive difficult times.
modern_application: The proverb applies to modern society through issues such as climate change, economic crises, public health, and security. Communities become stronger when people understand that their actions affect others.
